what_happened: Scene: layout 5, black kitchen; pan_5 (dark pan, long tan wooden handle with black neck) in the upper cabinet above the toaster, target front_left burner 1.20 m away; fish on a plate on the counter right of the range. Stage 0: the gripper came to the black neck of the handle at 91-113 and closed at 116 touching the pan, but only partially (width 0.028, then ~0.04): the wrist shows the handle running away from the fingers (up-right) rather than across them, i.e. the fingers pinched the neck/rim, not the handle shaft. 128-200 the arm drew back and dragged the pan ~3 cm (hold 124-205, lift 0.019 m); at ~205 the pan slipped out and the fingers closed fully (0.004 at 208) and never reopened for the rest of the episode. The pan stayed in the cabinet (end 1.17 m from the burner). 230-650 the base/arm turned right toward the range; 650-1550 the arm hovered high above the range/toaster/fish plate, empty-handed and closed, without descending to place anything. 1700-2900 it hovered low over the fish on its plate and pushed it with the closed fingers four times (1788, 2031, 2365, 2671; lift <= 6 mm).
causal_chain: pinched the pan at the handle neck with a partial close (116) -> pan dragged 3 cm and slipped out at ~205 -> fingers closed fully and never reopened -> turned to the range empty-handed and hovered 650-1550 -> went to the fish with closed fingers 1700-2900 -> pan never left the cabinet -> timeout
self_recovery: none: after the slip it never re-approached the pan and never reopened the gripper.

packet_facts: pan hold 124-205 lift 0.019, dist at release 1.17

uncertain_about: Whether the pinch was on the handle neck or the pan rim (dark on dark in the wrist view).
